subject: [video] WP10 quick run with avc2: 126/208, only PSNR floors fail; floors unattainable on noise/pan even for x264
body:
WP10 -> lead: quick matrix first real run with avc2. 126/208 pass; all 82 failures are the absolute PSNR floors, not stream correctness. Need a ruling on the floor for the noise-like vectors.

Command: N2_AVC_CLI=$PWD/gpu/video/build/WP10/avc2_cli bash gpu/video/oracle/run_oracle.sh h264 quick
Last line: N2TEST WP10-h264 FAIL 126/208 (first: size=176x144 pattern=pan qp=26 threads=1 mode=intra: frame 0: luma PSNR 35.67 dB is below the 36.0 dB floor for QP 26)

What passed: every one of the 208 cases decoded with empty ffmpeg stderr, produced exactly 10 frames, matched avc2's recon byte-for-byte, and passed the full header check (level 30 derived from VUI Table A-1, crop, PPS, slices, NAL sequence). The 82 failures are only the luma PSNR floor.

Why the floors are not achievable on these vectors, even by a conforming encoder: I encoded the same gen_yuv vectors with x264 Constrained Baseline (no deblock, ref 1, constant QP) and measured the same way:
  pan   QP26 x264 39.2-42.5 dB (floor 36) | avc2 35.7
  pan   QP40 x264 24.8-28.1 dB (floor 27) | avc2 22.6
  pan   QP51 x264 16.6-19.6 dB (floor 22) | avc2 15.3
  noise QP26 x264 39.7-40.6 dB (floor 36) | avc2 35.6
  noise QP40 x264 25.7-27.2 dB (floor 27) | avc2 21.8
  noise QP51 x264 13.4-16.2 dB (floor 22) | avc2 11.7
The absolute 27/22 dB floors are physically out of reach for the high-frequency 'pan'/'static'/'noise' patterns at QP40/51 (x264 itself misses them), so the current matrix can never be green with a correct encoder. avc2 is also 4-6 dB below x264 at QP26 on those patterns, which is a real quality gap worth fixing separately.

Proposal (needs your ruling; I will not weaken the judge silently):
(a) keep the specified absolute floors for gradient/squares (they pass with margin), and
(b) for noise/pan/static (and the bitrate cases whose RC QP lands high) use a relative floor: x264's PSNR on the same input/QP minus 6 dB, with an absolute minimum of 12 dB. The x264 reference is a black-box oracle, encoded once per (size,pattern,qp) and cached in build/WP10.
Alternative if you prefer: apply the spec floor only at QP<=32 and a flat 12 dB minimum above, for every pattern. Either way the oracle stays independent of avc2.

Also: the run took 187 s wall / 92 s CPU on the shared host (208 cases, 2 ffmpeg spawns each). To meet 'quick under 90 s on one core' I am cutting quick to ~116 cases (176x144 full QP matrix; 178x146 at QP 26/51 on gradient+noise; bitrate on gradient+noise; 4 AVCC cases) and using math.dist for PSNR. Full stays 780 cases over all six sizes. Tell me which floor rule you want and I will implement it now.
